opencode.text: The “untouched” holdout is vulnerable to overfitting if the same post‑2026‑06‑15 slice is repeatedly inspected or used to choose N/M/K, and a single time split does not establish robustness across regimes. The proposal also assumes the outcome log contains enough intratrade path data to replay time stops, breakeven moves, and realistic execution without lookahead; terminal outcomes alone cannot validate those counterfactual exits. “Win rate stays ≥60%” is an unnecessary optimization target, while costs, gap behavior, simultaneous SL triggers, and the definition of “manual” exits need explicit, testable replay semantics before promotion gates are meaningful.

proposals.text: Proposal: Run an exit-side research cycle targeting the measured payoff-geometry deficit in `outcome_learning.md` (win rate 67.5% yet expectancy −0.012 and PF 0.77 because avg_loss ≈ 3× avg_win, tail_loss 1.21 erases ~20 wins, SL closes run at exp −0.55, and 76% of exits are "manual" rather than automated). Concretely: use `bot/aegis/research/exit_research.py` to grid-test a hard time-stop plus breakeven-move rule (close any position not ≥ +N pips within M bars; move SL to entry at +K pips) over the existing 3,370-row reconciled outcome log with a time-split train/holdout like the ML filter used (train ≤ 2026-06-15, holdout after). Falsifiable prediction: on the untouched holdout, expectancy flips from −0.012 to > 0 with PF > 1 while win rate stays ≥ 60%, net of runner spread/slippage, and bootstrap 5th-percentile expectancy > 0 (the same criterion that rejected the ML filter candidate). If the holdout passes every gate in `promote.py` it becomes a governed challenger; if it fails, record the rejection in `ExperimentRegistry` and seal it per protocol. No code changes, no champion edit, no live YAML touched — this is a replay-based shadow experiment only, consistent with the expectancy-first framing in *Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom* (no direct corpus passages matched this case).

Test a challenger that abstains when the validated-state sample count is below a preregistered threshold, leaving all other champion logic unchanged. Evaluate it on the sealed holdout with identical spread/slippage assumptions and record the experiment; accept the candidate only if net expectancy improves by at least 5% without increasing maximum drawdown or reducing trade count by more than 20%. Otherwise reject it and retain the current champion unchanged.

question: The AEGIS MT5 DEMO bot is running the intelligent firehose with the validated-state gate. Given the current measured evidence, identify ONE concrete, falsifiable improvement candidate for the next research cycle. Do not modify code or the champion. Cite book corpus passages if relevant.

opencode.text: Proposal: Run an exit-side research cycle targeting the payoff-geometry deficit in `outcome_learning.md` (win rate 67.5% but expectancy −0.012 and PF 0.77, avg_loss ≈ 3× avg_win), using `bot/aegis/research/exit_research.py` over the reconciled outcome log joined with read-only M1 bar history. Before any simulation, verify the data actually supports intratrade replay (per-bar high/low around each position's entry/SL); if only terminal outcomes exist, record the data gap in `ExperimentRegistry` and stop rather than fabricate counterfactual paths. Replay semantics will be fixed and documented up front: triggers fill at the next bar open, every exit pays runner spread/slippage, gaps close at the first post-gap open with no favorable intra-gap SL assumption, simultaneous SL/time-stop conflicts resolve to the worse price, and "manual" exits are defined as those lacking an automated-rule match and are excluded from rule-attribution metrics. The N/M/K grid is chosen solely on train-period data (≤ 2026-06-15) via walk-forward folds spanning distinct regimes; the post-cutoff holdout is then evaluated exactly once on the single pre-registered config, with results committed before any further slicing. Promotion requires expectancy > 0, PF > 1, and bootstrap 5th-percentile expectancy > 0 net of costs on both the worst walk-forward fold and the untouched holdout (win rate reported diagnostically only), followed by every gate in `promote.py`; failure is recorded and sealed, with no code changes, no champion edits, and no live YAML touched.
